1. The Complete Path, at a Glance
blocks.text: 1. The Complete Path, at a Glance

blocks.content: Recapping the high-level workflow first introduced back in Module 1, but now with every stage's real internals in view: kubectl apply, the API server pipeline, an etcd write, the scheduler pipeline, kubelet's syncLoop, and finally a running, networked container.

blocks.alt: The entire path, every stage now backed by the real internals covered throughout this module

blocks.content: 2. Steps 1 to 2: kubectl and the API Server
blocks.text: 2. Steps 1 to 2: kubectl and the API Server

blocks.content: kubectl apply submits the manifest, which travels through the full five-stage API Server Request Flow covered earlier in this module, authentication, authorization, the two admission control sub-phases, before anything is even persisted.

blocks.alt: The full, five-stage pipeline from the API Server Request Flow topic, applied here concretely

blocks.content: Once past admission control, the new Pod's desired state is written to etcd, exactly the key-value structure and resourceVersion mechanics covered in the etcd Data Storage topic.

blocks.alt: The exact etcd storage mechanics covered in this module's dedicated topic

blocks.content: The scheduler notices the new, unassigned Pod and runs it through the full filtering, scoring, and binding pipeline covered in the Scheduler Workflow topic, writing its decision back through the API server, never touching the Pod directly.

blocks.alt: The complete three-stage pipeline from the Scheduler Workflow topic, applied here

blocks.content: The node's kubelet, watching for Pods assigned to it, notices this new one, its syncLoop creates the sandbox, calls the CNI plugin exactly as covered in the CNI Workflow topic, and the container runtime, covered in the Docker Internals module, finally starts the actual containers, PLEG confirms it, and status flows back to the API server, completing the loop.

blocks.alt: kubelet's syncLoop, sandbox creation, and CNI ADD, exactly as covered earlier in this module

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: This complete flow, apply, API server pipeline, etcd, scheduler pipeline, kubelet syncLoop, CNI, and finally a running container, ties together every internals topic covered in this module.
Understanding this full trace end to end is what lets you reason precisely about where in the pipeline any given failure or delay is actually happening.
